regions.text: at the solicitation of Japan, was still in
regions.explanation: From 29.27s to 31.48s (“at the solicitation of Japan, was still in”), articulation rate was 7.65 syll/s against 3.44 syll/s in the reference (+122%); that is 2.3× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Faster articulation compresses the stressed syllables and the micro-pauses listeners use to segment phrases, so key words lose emphasis and comprehension drops. Fix: Slow to the reference pace here and let the pauses between clauses breathe.

Fix: Keep this phrase in one breath; pause at the punctuation instead.

regions.text: Japan makes it obvious that the attack was deliberately planned many days
regions.explanation: From 99.98s to 108.01s (“Japan makes it obvious that the attack was deliberately …”), the share of energy above 2 kHz dropped to 3.7% from 25.4% (-86%); that is 8.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Energy above 2 kHz carries consonant bursts and fricatives (t, k, s, f); losing it blurs word boundaries and makes the speech sound muffled even at normal volume. Fix: Open the mouth more and finish final consonants crisply.

regions.text: makes it obvious that the attack was deliberately planned many
regions.explanation: From 101.81s to 107.16s (“makes it obvious that the attack was deliberately planned …”), loudness relative to the speaker's own level fell 6.3 dB below the reference, bottoming out 8.9 dB down; that is 1.3× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. The loudness falls away across the phrase, so its final words - often the payoff - drop toward the noise floor of the room. Fix: Support the breath through the end of the phrase; the last words need the same energy as the first.
